prompt_context_by_prefix.lpn:
Use these preferred technical term translations when relevant:
- flow (Q): caudal
- velocity (v): velocidad
- slope (S): pendiente
    DO NOT render as: activity/fitness sense of 'grade' — the treadmill or trail incline for running/walking/jogging; this is the hydraulic energy gradient, not an exercise setting; geographic or topographic landform term; school grade / academic mark

lpn.context: Volumetric flow rate. Appears in every calculator. Use the hydraulic/civil engineering term for discharge volume per unit time, not a general word for 'water flowing'.
lpn.translation_notes: Spanish has two common terms: 'caudal' (Spain, South America) and 'gasto' (Mexico). Lead with 'caudal'. Portuguese: 'vazão' (Brazil) or 'caudal' (Portugal) — lead with 'vazão'. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'protok/protoka' — consistent with current glossary entries (confirmed match). bg RESOLVED (Tom, 2026-07-13): native engineer's 2026-07-06 clarification confirmed both 'дебит' (colloquial/general register) and 'водно количество' (academic/hydraulic-engineering register, used at university for Q) are acceptable. Tom decided suite-wide standardization on 'водно количество' — "I would put водно количество everywhere" — applied across all bg calculator categories (pipes/irrigation included, not just the hydraulic-structure/open-channel strings the engineer originally corrected). 'дебит' fully replaced in lib/lang.ec.bg.php 2026-07-13. Task 109 stages 3-5 (2026-07-19): bg standardized on водно количество (дебит drift removed from or_/mpf_/cs_ per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md); sr standardized on проток (stage 4); it confirmed on portata (flusso drift removed).

lpn.context: Flow velocity (speed of water). Appears in all calculators.
lpn.translation_notes: Most languages use a direct cognate of 'velocity'. Do not use a word meaning 'speed' in a general sense if a more precise hydraulic term exists. Pre-2026 sr/hr human translations used 'tečenja' (= flowing, a verbal noun from 'teći' = to flow) — this is less precise than the current 'brzina/брзина' (= speed/velocity) and the current AI-generated term is preferred.

lpn.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
lpn.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses.

keys_to_translate.lpn_main_title: PREVIEW: Free Online Looped Pipe Network Calculator with Map Interface
keys_to_translate.lpn_main_desc: PREVIEW — Pressure and Flow in a Looped Pipe Network You Draw on a Map
keys_to_translate.lpn_preview_banner: PREVIEW — This calculator is new and still changing. It is in English only for now. See the Notes below for current limits. Comments and suggestions are always welcome.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_elev_tip: Ground or pipe level at this node. Measure it from any zero you like, as long as every node uses the same one.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_head_tip: Water surface level in the reservoir, measured as a height, not as a pressure. Leave it blank to put the water surface at the reservoir elevation.
keys_to_translate.lpn_empty_hint: To start, use the toolbar to add a background image or a reservoir, or to draw an example network.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_example: This adds the example to the network you already have. Continue?
keys_to_translate.lpn_demand_tip: Flow taken out of the network at this node. Enter a negative number for flow put into the network here.
keys_to_translate.lpn_result_gradient_tip: Head loss divided by the length of the pipe. Use it to compare pipes of different lengths against one design limit.
keys_to_translate.lpn_result_head_tip: Energy of the water at this node, written as a height of water column. It is a height, not a pressure.
keys_to_translate.lpn_tool_clear_tip: Empties this project: the drawing, the background image, and the project name. Your settings and your other projects are not changed.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_restore_tip: Resets this project's settings only. Your drawing and your other projects are not changed.
keys_to_translate.lpn_reset_all_tip: Deletes every project, every background image, every setting, and your unit choices, then reloads the page exactly as a first-time visitor sees it. This is the only reset that clears everything.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_clear: This permanently deletes the network, the background image, and the project name. Your settings are kept. Continue?
keys_to_translate.lpn_storage_too_new: This project was saved by a newer version of the page, so it cannot be opened here.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_project_delete: Delete this project and everything in it? This cannot be undone.
keys_to_translate.lpn_status_deleted_empty: Deleted {deleted}. Started a new empty project.
keys_to_translate.lpn_storage_full: Not saved. Browser storage is full or unavailable, so your recent changes will be lost when you close this tab.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_1_def: Solves one set of demands at a time, using the same gradient method EPANET uses. It does not model how the network changes over time.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_2_def: Tanks, water quality, and control valves that open and close on their own (PRV, PSV, FCV) are not modeled. A pipe can carry a fixed minor loss, but not a valve whose open or closed state depends on the flow being solved for.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_3_def: Your projects are saved automatically in this browser, and nowhere else. Clearing your browser data deletes them, and a project cannot yet be written to a file or moved to another device. Because this is an early preview, please use it for small networks and for testing only.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_5_def: A pump follows H = H₀ − aQ^b, where H is the head the pump adds and Q is the flow through it. Enter one, two, or three points from the manufacturer's curve. Three points — the head at zero flow, the normal working point, and the point of highest flow — fit H₀, a and b directly, and follow a published curve most closely. Two points fit a parabola (b = 2) with its peak at zero flow. One point uses a common rule: the head at zero flow is 1.33 × the head you enter, and the highest flow is 2 × the flow you enter, which again gives b = 2. A pump with no points entered adds no head at all. The curve is not stopped at zero, so asking a pump for more flow than its curve can deliver gives a negative head. The fix is a bigger pump or a smaller demand, not a different curve fit.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_4_def: Writing a project to a file, and moving one between devices, are planned. Comments and suggestions are always welcome (see the feedback link above).
keys_to_translate.lpn_id_invalid: Enter an ID with no spaces and no quotation marks.
keys_to_translate.lpn_id_taken: That ID is already in use.
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_no_fixed_head: Add a reservoir. The network needs at least one known water level before it can be solved.
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_dangling_link: A pipe or pump connects to a node that no longer exists:
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_unreachable: These nodes have no path to a reservoir:
keys_to_translate.lpn_diag_not_converged: No solution was found. Check for values that cannot be real, such as a diameter of zero.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_roughness_tip: Hazen-Williams C. A higher number means a smoother pipe: about 150 for new plastic, 130 for new steel or iron, and 100 for old pipe.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_length_tip: Length of the pipe. With Auto turned on this follows what you drew. Turn Auto off to type a length that differs from the drawing.
keys_to_translate.lpn_field_km_tip: Loss from the bends, valves, and fittings on this pipe, counted as a multiple of the velocity head. Use 0 for a plain straight pipe.
keys_to_translate.lpn_pump_curve_ref_note: Using the curve entered for pump {id}.
keys_to_translate.lpn_pump_curve_note: One, two, or three points — see "Pump curve" in the Notes below.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_select: Mode: Select. Click an element or a label to see or change it. Drag to move a node, a vertex, or a label. Double-click a pipe to add or remove a vertex.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_delete: Mode: Delete. Click an element to remove it.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_junction: Mode: Add Junction. Click the map to place a junction. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_reservoir: Mode: Add Reservoir. Click the map to place a reservoir. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_pipe: Mode: Add Pipe. Click a node, then another node, to connect them. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_pump: Mode: Add Pump. Click a node, then another node, to connect them. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_mode_add_text: Mode: Add Text. Click the map to place a text label. Click near a node to attach the text to that node. Switch to Select mode to change or move elements and labels.
keys_to_translate.lpn_tip_select: Use this mode to change, move, and drag things on the map.
keys_to_translate.lpn_tip_labels_draggable: You can drag a label to move it. Double-click a label to put it back.
keys_to_translate.lpn_labels_decimals_tip: Decimal places shown for this label
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_scale_prompt1: Click two points on the background image, such as the two ends of a bar scale. Then type the real distance between them.
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_scale_prompt2: Real distance between the two points
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_position_prompt1: Click any point on the background image. This is the point you will move.
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_position_prompt2: Choose where that point should go, then click Continue.
keys_to_translate.lpn_backdrop_coords_prompt: Type the X,Y that point should move to
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_defaults_note: Used for elements you create from now on. Existing elements are not changed.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_push_note: Only the properties whose labels are showing right now are applied.
keys_to_translate.lpn_push_confirm: Replace these properties on every existing element with the current default inputs? Values you have typed will be overwritten. You can undo this.
keys_to_translate.lpn_push_none_displayed: No default input is showing as a label right now, so there is nothing to apply. Turn on the labels for the properties you want in the Labels panel, then try again.
keys_to_translate.lpn_push_nothing: No existing element has any of the properties being applied.
keys_to_translate.lpn_push_no_change: Every element already has these values, so nothing would change.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_tolerance_tip: How close the solver has to get before it stops. A smaller number is more exact and takes longer.
keys_to_translate.lpn_settings_map_height_tip: On a small screen the map is drawn shorter than this, so that part of the page is always left to scroll.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_restore_defaults: Reset all settings (ID prefixes, default inputs, solver settings, map display, legend position, and visible labels) to their defaults? Your network is not changed. Settings belong to the open project, so your other projects keep their own.
keys_to_translate.lpn_confirm_wipe: Delete EVERYTHING saved for this page — every project, every background image, all settings, and your unit choices — and reload the page as a brand-new visitor would see it? This cannot be undone.
